chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: European vogue for ragtime; six months at Philharmonic Hall
summary: Jim Europe and regimental bands had created a vogue for ragtime in Europe; the orchestra played nightly with matinees at Philharmonic Hall, Great Portland Street, for six months.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, there was a lot of interest in Europe in American music, at that time?
Oh yes, everything. Everything, yes.
Briggs
Don't forget you had the Jim Europe band. The Jim Europe band played more ragtime than anything else.
Yes.

You see. And not only -- I'm just saying Jim Europe, 'cause I don't know the names of others, but regimental bands, all colors, they played the same. Still more or less the same music, the same music.
Ragtime, a lot of ragtime?
Oh, yes. They played a lot of ragtime. A lot of ragtime.
So there was kind of a vogue for this sort of thing in Europe.
Oh, yes, a vogue, yes, sure.
So then Lattimore was able to book you.--
He booked us at the
Briggs
Philharmonic Hall for six solid months.
The Philharmonic Hall?
Yes, Great Portland Street.
And what, you were there every night for six months?
Every night and we had two matinees. We had a matinee on Sunday afternoon. We had regular concerts every night, and two matinees a week, Saturdays and Sundays.
For six months in the same place?
Six months in the same place.
Wow. Then what? Then you had to keep getting new arrangements.
Oh, yes, we had to change the repertory. Change the repertory. Yes, there were singers and everything, they'd change the repertory.
